title: E2E default-branch and protected Production promotion classification

phases.objective: Classify trusted default-branch execution, declared parallel pull requests, and governed Production promotions without inheriting unrelated pull-request identity or weakening fail-closed branch rules.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: The parallel PR flow self-test invokes the canonical E2E PR gate in isolated synthetic Git contexts.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Default-branch/manual execution is standard, declared workstreams retain bounded classification, undeclared PR branches fail closed, and only exact protected or immutable main-derived Production identities are accepted.
steps: Create a synthetic repository baseline and bind local and remote main refs.
Remove inherited pull-request base/head environment variables for the default-branch fixture.
Invoke the canonical gate for main without a PR base ref and require standard mode.
Invoke the gate for an undeclared branch with an Integration base and require bounded rejection.
Retain workstream-to-Integration enforcement and direct workstream-to-main rejection.
Retain exact main-to-Production and immutable main-snapshot promotion acceptance with spoof rejection.
assertions: Default-branch/manual execution does not inherit enclosing pull-request identity.
The undeclared-branch guard executes only when a pull-request base ref exists.
Declared workstream and Integration rules remain fail closed.
Merge-queue refs remain excluded from ordinary PR classification.
Protected main and SHA-bound immutable main snapshots remain the only accepted Production promotion identities.
No repository write, protected-ref update, deployment, provider call, credential read, SQL, migration Apply, database mutation, or external send occurs.

phases.objective: Observe the classifier across protected pull requests, workflow dispatches, default-branch runs, and immutable Production release snapshots using canonical structured E2E evidence.
Retain bounded diagnostics for inherited environment variables, missing refs, spoofed promotion identities, stale SHAs, and malformed parallel-work contracts.
Validate one non-production default-branch/manual run, one declared parallel pull-request flow, and one immutable Production snapshot classification.
Require exact classifier evidence for protected main-to-Production and immutable main-snapshot promotions without granting merge or deployment authority.
